item.title: Burden of Proof
item.description: A lot of information is consumed without the consumers ever probing its origins or motives, and asking if it makes sense logically. They consume it by faith because it comes from “credible” sources. Credible: mainstream, sponsored, etc. For example, in geographical science, the theory that the earth is a globe, even though this phenomenon contradicts simple observatory evidence. You learn that the earth rotates and revolves, yet you see the sun and moon moves above you, and do not sense the earth move. Another example, modern history is a narrative of the elites of today. Ancient history is also written, not in full, to support or drive a certain agenda.

item.title: What Is (Even) True?
item.description:
A lot of the content we already consume is AI-generated. This AI machinery is made available to the commoner (supposedly by the elite) to play around with, and the end result is a less functional human being — one that is unable to think. But this did not start recently.

From an imperial point of view, the colonial masters collected all that had been amalgamated during the Age of Enlightenment and construed an education system based on it. After invading other lands, they covered up heinous acts from the history books they wrote. For half a century, we have fed our minds with lies, half-lies and narratives controlled by these people.
